body:
Is it possible that for Godot 4.5dev5:

The PCK Templates need to be generated with NDK27,
and then Godot's final Build will use NDK28 automatically to make the app... 
-> thus solving the 16kb Memory problem with Android 14/15??


"Android: Add support for 16 KB page sizes, update to NDK r28b ([GH-106358](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106358))."

Godot 4.5 dev 5 official builds were made with NDK r28b, so it should work.

It works fine in my tests locally on Fedora 42, and works on CI.

So the problem must be on your end. I would suggest removing your manually installed NDK, and let Godot's buildsystem install it automatically when you compile.

Thanks for the heads up, and confirmation!

However, I thought generating PCK Encrypted Templates was a necessary and crucial step for the app's protection/security..  
isn't that the case??

I thought using Encryption with normal templates will not work;
and if you want to secure the app/assets on Android to any extent, building Encrypted Export Templates is essential.

Doesnt PCK Encryption with a 256-bit AES key ensure assets are protected??

I thought this system will protect the code/assets from being easily extracted/decompiled, 
as without encryption, tools like gdsdecomp can expose the entire project, including GDScript with comments,
posing a significant risk, like unauthorized Redistribution...

This requires building Custom PCK Encrypted Export Templates with the same export key, to work, 
as normal templates won’t support it.

Simply setting a PCK key in the export dialog doesn’t provide protection unless custom templates are compiled with the same key, 
as per the Godot documentation. 


-So I guess you might be referring to standard normal exports with NDK r28b, 
which don’t use PCK encryption unless custom templates are built.

Right?

Godot 4.5dev5 will surely use NDK28 on final build, if it's configured/made that way.

But the Encryption will not be effective unless you generate and use proper PCK Encrypted Templates.

And that's the problem:
PCK Encrypted Template Generation seems to be broken atm..


Any insights on making SCons works with NDK28’s Clang++ for Godot 4.5dev5 Encrypted Template generation would be greatly appreciated.

What I'm saying is that compiling Godot with NDK r28b works fine for me, clang and clang++ are found and usable.

Adding an encryption key shouldn't impact that, it's the exact same build process, with just some extra Python code to generate a header with the encryption key.

- Generating custom templates is necessary if you want to use PCK encryption.
- Default Android export doesn't use PCK, and therefore does not support PCK encryption. It's only supported if APK expansion is enabled.
- Encryption can be easily worked around, so is the absolute minimum level of protection.

"I would suggest removing your manually installed NDK, and let Godot's build system install it automatically when you compile."

-I'm reading contradictory things about this aspect of Encryption and APK Expansion.

Is it possible that:
In Older version of Godot PCK Encryption itself did Not work standalone, and it needed to have APK Expansion too?

And now in Newer versions of Godot like 4.4 or 4.5, PCK Encryption is indeed working to a good extent?


-And then > If normal PCK Encryption is working on its own in newer version of Godot...
I guess adding the APK Expansion on top, will add an extra layer of protection, by having all the assets on the OBB files??


-What's necessary in order to ensure a proper APK Expansion config?

Afaik would be like:
Go to Google Console "Test & Release / Setup / App Signing" and download the "App signing key certificate",
this gives you a file called: "deployment_cert.der"

Then you can extract the contents with:
openssl x509 -in "COM deployment_cert.der" -inform der -fingerprint -sha256 -noout
sha256 Fingerprint= 

In Sha256 Fingerprint you put the SHA-256 certificate fingerprint number from Google Conole.

This generates a PEM file that you can read, kinda like:
-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
... keycharacters ....
-----END PUBLIC KEY-----


-So you go to Godot Export:
Enable APK Expansion
Copy the Public key.

Do we need to ad a Salt string??
Yes or No?

And then we just export the app in AAB format with:
PCK Encryption Key
APK Expansion Enabled + Public Key (+ Salt?)

And then we sign it, with our usual keysignature,
and then it's 100% ready for Google Console?

>
> And now in Newer versions of Godot like 4.4 or 4.5, PCK Encryption is indeed working to a good extent?

None of the versions support encryption without APK expansion. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105984 adds support for it.

I finally managed to generate all PCK Templates from Godot 4.5dev5 source..

Thank you for the Patience and advice.

-In the end I had to rescue the generated .so files, as something made them dissapear instantly.
But once a template is made, remaking it is a matter of seconds..

rm -rf bin/obj/ && rm -f bin/*.* && mkdir -p bin/obj
scons platform=android arch=arm64 target=template_release production=yes module_mono_enabled=yes
if [ ! -f bin/libgodot.android.template_release.arm64.so ]; then scons platform=android arch=arm64 target=template_release production=yes module_mono_enabled=yes; fi
cp bin/libgodot.android.template_release.arm64.so ../godot_temp_libs/

This ensured the files were saved,
and then everything is set clean before doing the next template, etc..

Now I'm exporting the app with Godot 4.5dev5 and proper PCK Templates, 
so that's an advancement!
